messages.subject: ddply question
parts:

Anyone know the meaning of this message:

tst <- data.frame(x=c(rep('a',100),rep('b',200)),y=rnorm(300))
tst.avg <- ddply(tst,.(x),summarize,y=mean(y))

Error: 'by' is missing


Seems like my plyr is messed up, but I'm not sure. Any suggestions how to get it working again? Thanks.
       

Adam Loveland

parts: Adam,

Anyone know the meaning of this message:

tst <- data.frame(x=c(rep('a',100),rep('b',200)),y=rnorm(300))

Like Brandon, I don't get this error.

However, if you look here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3277326/group-by-in-r-ddply-with-weighted-mean

there is reference to a very similar error (Error in is.list(by) : 'by' is missing)
occurring in one of the answers and prompted this comment from someone
known as Fr:
<quote>
I'm getting that error too on similar code. The error occurs only in RStudio. It's due to Hmisc::summarize being higher than plyr::ddply in the search() list. See this link‌​. Fix it by replacing summarize with summarise: it works and does not create a conflict with Hmisc. Welcome to dependency hell!
</quote>

Might be helpful?

Ron.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ddply question
parts:
I ran into this problem back in 2010 (Hmisc:summarize masking plyr:summarize) so I've avoided the problem since by using the Commonwealth spelling in plyr. This isn't an uncommon event because a number of R packages depend on Hmisc, so it could easily happen that Hmisc winds up ahead of plyr in the package hierarchy without you noticing it.

The speed with which Hadley responded to my question at the time made me realize this is a plyr FAQ. And as Adam mentioned, this is an issue of function masking which has nothing whatsoever to do with RStudio. If you want to continue using summarize(), the safe way to do it is to prepend the package name so that the evaluator (and you) know which package in which to look for it. Returning to Adam's example,

library(plyr)
library(Hmisc)      # Hmisc ahead of plyr in the package hierarchy
search()

tst <- data.frame(x=rep(c(100, 200), times = c(3, 5)), y=rnorm(8)) 
ddply(tst, .(x), summarize, y=mean(y))    # Error due to masking of plyr's summarize()
ddply(tst, "x", plyr::summarize, y = mean(y))   # Works

Dennis

On Fri, Oct 3, 2014 at 7:29 AM, <adam.l...@pnc.com> wrote:
Awesome! Thanks. That fixed it! I should mention I'm not in R-studio, so evidently, it's not just a problem there.

These kinds of bugs aren't really a big deal in my opinion, given the flow of information we have amongst users on groups like this one.

Thanks again.



Adam

Hi Vivek:

I'm afraid dplyr doesn't absolve you from masking issues, which was the point of the post:

library(dplyr)
library(Hmisc)   # see the startup message

# This produces an error:

tst <- data.frame(x=rep(c(100, 200), times = c(3, 5)), y=rnorm(8)) 
tst %>% group_by(x) %>% summarize(y=mean(y))

# These work:

tst %>% group_by(x) %>% dplyr::summarize(y = mean(y))
tst %>% group_by(x) %>% summarise(y = mean(y))  # no conflict with Hmisc


Dennis
